html:
The Maitrakas ruled Gujarat from their capital Valabhi on the Saurashtra peninsula from about 475 to 776.

The founder, Bhatarka, was a general of the Gupta Empire who made himself independent as Gupta power fell. His heirs ruled most of Gujarat and parts of Malwa. One of them, Dhruvasena II, married a daughter of Harsha.

Valabhi was a centre of learning. The Chinese pilgrim Yijing ranked its Buddhist monasteries with Nalanda, and in the 5th century a council of Jain monks met at Valabhi to write down their scriptures. The port grew rich on sea trade. The dynasty ended around 776, probably after raids by the Arabs of Sindh.
sum: The Maitrakas ruled Gujarat from their capital Valabhi on the Saurashtra peninsula from about 475 to 776.
